inputs.original_text: The owner of Blue Waters has said that Government collects taxes from them “without doing or investing in anything”.Perhaps this might be considered as an environmental tax. Plastic bottles can be found everywhere, blocking rivers and drains, which then enter...
inputs.modified_text: The owner of Blue Waters is right to question a government that collects taxes while plastic bottles choke rivers and drains. Calling another charge an “environmental tax” doesn’t excuse failure to deliver basic services—or guarantee that the money will be used well. But no tax can replace personal responsibility: businesses and citizens alike must stop treating public spaces as someone else’s problem. Clean communities depend on accountable government and respect for the standards that keep shared spaces orderly.
